text:
liam: Quick flag from model onboarding: atlas-rerank shows ndcg@10 down ~2.6% on goldset_holdout but mrr@10 up ~0.9%. Baseline vs new model looks dataset-sensitive. Anyone else see dataset-choice effects?
sara: Which holdout did you run exactly? goldset vs silverset? We sometimes default to silver for quicker runs.
liam: Ran both. Command: `./bench/rerank_eval --model atlas-rerank-v2 --sets goldset_holdout,silverset_sample --metrics ndcg@10,mrr@10 --seed 11`
devin: Paste the raw numbers?
sara: Baseline (prod-ranker):
```
goldset_holdout -> ndcg@10 0.4582  mrr@10 0.2541
silverset_sample -> ndcg@10 0.4235  mrr@10 0.2370
```
liam: New model (after onboarding PR):
```
goldset_holdout -> ndcg@10 0.4460  mrr@10 0.2623
silverset_sample -> ndcg@10 0.4221  mrr@10 0.2390
```
devin: Interesting: silverset barely moved, goldset dropped more. That implies dataset composition and formatting differences amplify the signal.
tia: What diffs between goldset and silverset? Goldset has human-curated anchors, longer passage contexts, and keeps HTML markup in candidates. Silverset is synthetic, passage-trimmed and HTML-stripped.
sara: We changed candidate-snippet formatting in the PR to strip inner HTML and collapse lists. That would affect goldset more since humans relied on visual separators.
eval-bot: scheduled-ablation: run-id rb-4301. Matrix: dataset=goldset/silverset, format=doc/passage, html=keep/strip, normalize=old/new, quant=fp16/int8. ETA ~22m. :gear:
devin: Also check dedupe/pruning thresholds; goldset has more near-duplicates so dedupe interacts with formatting.
liam: I ran a quick per-query churn sample: on goldset 28/200 queries show >3 position swaps in top10; silverset only 6/200.
tia: Good tracer. If HTML/formatting removal collapses headings/lists into inline text, embeddings shift and mid-tail ordering breaks (ndcg). MRR can increase if the very best passage becomes clearer.
sara: eval-bot posted early ablation snapshot:
```
goldset format=doc html=keep normalize=old quant=fp16 -> ndcg@10 0.4582 mrr@10 0.2541
goldset format=doc html=strip normalize=new quant=fp16 -> ndcg@10 0.4460 mrr@10 0.2623
goldset format=passage html=strip normalize=new quant=fp16 -> ndcg@10 0.4491 mrr@10 0.2600
silverset format=passage html=strip normalize=new quant=fp16 -> ndcg@10 0.4221 mrr@10 0.2390
goldset format=doc html=strip normalize=new quant=int8  -> ndcg@10 0.4432 mrr@10 0.2639
```
devin: From that table: stripping HTML + new normalize is the worst for goldset doc format. Passage format helps a bit. int8 quant slightly worsens ndcg but raises mrr. Classic signature.
tia: Root cause hypothesis: goldset ranking relies on structural cues in HTML (headings, bullets). Stripping them flattens semantics, hurting reordering but occasionally clarifying top hit.
liam: Proposed actions: 1) Add an HTML-preserve toggle for goldset-like flows and re-run canary. 2) Add a dedicated goldset parity check in the onboarding checklist. 3) Produce per-query examples showing HTML->stripped diffs for >3 position swaps (devin).
sara: I'll open a small PR to make HTML stripping conditional per dataset and add a gating rule: goldset_holdout must pass ndcg parity within 1% before canary.
eval-bot: note: rolling up detailed run artifacts to /runs/rb-4301; churn CSV and diff snippets available.
devin: I'll generate an embed-drift histogram and a tiny visualization for product to see which structural tokens are losing weight.
tia: Also recommend running a small A/B in dedicated with html=keep for a subset of users if product agrees.
liam: Thanks all. Blocking promotion until goldset parity fixed. Will follow up after regen runs. :lock:
